data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 demands representational separation (different tokenizers/geometries) as necessary for independence, but this is stronger than the problem requires and is self-undermined by its own analogy. SRC_001 notes that a formal proof checker can verify a human's proof without sharing representation — yet a proof checker shares the same formal system (inference rules, axioms, definitions) as the proof author. If shared formal system does not defeat independence there, then SRC_001 never identifies why shared tokenization/attention specifically defeats it, other than asserting 'systematic errors transfer.' But its own perturbation test (feed the checker a notation variant the generator mishandled) is a within-single-engine, within-single-run test that could demonstrate independence — directly contradicting SRC_001's own necessity claim for engine separation. The target thus supplies the very counterexample its stated position must rule out.
